card.name: Frog species lists before Latin names
card.fires_on: Punctuation or digits right after a frog common name or an extinction year, just before a Latin species name or place name follows. Mostly in web text about amphibians, extinctions and place descriptions.

modes.label: Comma after frog name
modes.description: The comma after a frog's common name, where the Latin binomial comes next.

modes.label: Extinction or last-seen year
modes.description: A space or digit inside a year like 1983 or 1985 in text about species dying out.
modes.example: astric brooding frog, Australia. 2 species – Rheobatrachus vitellinus and R. silus, last seen 1<<9>>85.

modes.label: Place and census details
modes.description: A word or digit in location or census text, ahead of a place name or year.
modes.example: As of the census of <<2>>000, there were 6

card.writes: It promotes odd name fragments such as 'assin', 'baum' and 'ippi' and suppresses sand and desert words, so it points toward proper-name continuations.
card.plain: It fires in lists of rare frogs and places, just before a Latin or place name is due.
